title: Admissibility of gaps in infinite-time decision times
formal: In the specified ITTM model, is every nonzero limit ordinal beginning a bounded gap in the spectrum of least countable decision times admissible?
definitions:
Use parameter-free infinite-time Turing programs with a read-only binary input tape, a binary work tape and a binary output tape, indexed by the natural numbers, and one common head initially at cell 0. The work and output tapes are initially zero. A finite transition table reads the three current bits, writes the work/output bits, moves left or right (left at 0 stays at 0), and changes state. There are distinguished start, limit and halt states. At a successor stage execute one transition; entering halt ends the run at that stage. At a nonzero limit stage each writable cell takes the limsup of its earlier values, the head resets to 0 and the state becomes limit; the input is unchanged. The first output cell is the answer bit. No real, ordinal or oracle parameter is supplied. Finite integers may be hard-coded in the program. Inputs range over all x∈2^ω of the ambient universe V, not merely constructible reals. Countable means countable in V. For a total decider p let T(p)=sup_{x∈2^ω}t_p(x). For a decidable set A let δ(A)=min{T(p):p decides A}. Define the spectrum S={δ(A):A⊆2^ω is decidable and δ(A)<ω_1}. These are least times of sets, not the times of arbitrary padded programs. A bounded limit-start gap is a pair α<β<ω_1 such that α is a nonzero limit ordinal, sup(S∩α)=α, S∩[α,β)=∅ and β∈S. Thus the lower endpoint is approached by attainable times, is not itself attainable, and β is the first attainable time above it. The proposition quantifies over every such pair.

The constructible hierarchy is L_0=∅, L_{α+1}=Def(L_α), and L_λ=⋃_{α<λ}L_α at limits; Def takes all first-order definable subsets with parameters from the given level. An ordinal α is admissible here when L_α satisfies Kripke–Platek set theory with Infinity: Extensionality, Empty Set, Pairing, Union, Infinity, Foundation (set induction), Δ_0 Separation and Δ_0 Collection. Δ_0 formulas have only quantifiers bounded by sets.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof that every bounded limit-start gap (α,β) has L_α admissible, or a counterexample with proofs of all gap conditions and failure of admissibility. A theorem for clockable ordinals, arbitrary program times, or semidecision times alone does not answer this selected decision-time proposition.
context: Question 6.3 motivates the gap-admissibility question. Exact ordinal values depend on the machine convention, unlike agreement on computable functions.
why: A positive theorem would connect gaps in computational time spectra to the structure of admissible set theory.

import_provenance.original_title: Admissibility of gaps in infinite-time decision times
import_provenance.original_statement: Must every ordinal beginning a gap in the attainable countable decision times, or in the attainable countable semidecision times, be admissible? Here a set’s time is the least uniform supremum of halting times among its infinite-time algorithms.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The analogous theorem for clockable ordinals does not settle these decision-time spectra.

context_blocks.text: Question 6.3 motivates the gap-admissibility question. Exact ordinal values depend on the machine convention, unlike agreement on computable functions.

sentences: The spectrum records the fastest uniform decision time of each decidable set.
A gap contains no spectrum element and ends at an attainable time.
This variant requires a limit lower endpoint approached by attainable times.
Admissibility means that the corresponding constructible level satisfies KP with Infinity.
The decision-only limsup/reset formulation is explicitly separated from clockable and semidecision spectra.
